newsitem.title: UK: CBI urges UK to challenge EU emissions targets.
newsitem.headline: CBI urges UK to challenge EU emissions targets.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry on Friday urged the government to challenge proposed European Union (EU) targets for greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

"The EU targets do not appear to be based on an adequate assessment of the trade off between environmental and economic impacts, and demand higher reductions from the UK than those of most other member states," Adair Turner, director-general of the CBI, said in a statement.

The targets are due to be discussed on March 3 and 4, when the EU Environment Council will consider proposals from the Dutch presidency to reduce EU greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to 15 percent below 1990 levels by 2010.

The proposal would mean different targets for member states, with some expected to make further reductions to offset growth in others, the CBI said. UK emissions would have to fall by 20 percent, the fifth largest reduction and far removed from the British government's own proposal of a 5 to 10 percent reduction.
The CBI said Turner has written to Britain's Environment Secretary John Gummer expressing doubts over the targets.
In a separate statement, the CBI also called for full business participation in developing response policies and measures on climate change.
"British business has made a significant contribution to meeting current climate change commitments and will be instrumental in helping the UK to meet any future targets," it said.

The CBI said strengthening understanding of the economic implications of response options, establishing a longer-term framework for responses with the aim of stabilising greenhouse gas concentrations and securing world-wide agreement on policies and measures were among its priorities.
It said international negotiations are under way to secure agreement for post-2000 greenhouse gas reduction targets in December 1997, in Kyoto, Japan.
